bib.title: Igniting Language Intelligence: The Hitchhiker's Guide From Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Language Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Igniting Language Intelligence: The Hitchhiker's Guide From Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Language Agents", Zhuosheng Zhang, Yao Yao, Aston Zhang, Xiangru Tang, Xinbei Ma, Zhiwei He, Yiming Wang, Mark Gerstein, Rui Wang, Gongshen Liu, Hai Zhao (SJTU / AWS / Yale). Preprint (survey), 2023 (data "as of October 2023"). File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/03-agentic-foundations/sources/zhang-2023-igniting-language-intelligence.pdf

COVERAGE: All 37 pages, about 152,000 chars extracted. Body (pp.1-25, abstract through conclusion) read in full. Pages 26-37 are references only, skimmed. There is no appendix. Extraction is clean, apart from Fig 1 text and Fig 3 bars, which are images or garbled. Fig 3 bar values are not in the text, so I have not reported them.

CLAIMS (ranked for the tool-use / ReAct / CoT-to-agents note)

1. CoT works under two conditions: model size and relevant, interconnected parametric knowledge.
 number: 20 billion parameters
 setup: authors' synthesis of Wei 2023b, Tay 2022, Prystawski & Goodman 2023. Not a new experiment. Wei's three engineering conditions: a large LM, a multi-step task, and flat direct-prompting scaling.
 quote: "CoT demonstrates efficacy under two overarching conditions: first, when an LLM with preferably at least 20 billion parameters is employed, and second, when the parametric knowledge within the LLM encompasses knowledge pieces that are (i) pertinent to the task at hand and (ii) maintain strong mutual interconnections."
 where: p.3 (takeaways) and p.6 (Sec 3.1)

2. CoT is less effective on simple-step tasks and on small models, where it can hallucinate.
 number: none
 quote: "CoT reasoning is also less effective in simple-step tasks such as matching, sequence labeling (Qin et al., 2023a), and single-choice question (Chen et al., 2023a)."
 where: p.5

3. CoT elicits reasoning the model already has, rather than teaching it.
 number: "over 80-90%"
 setup: cited from Wang et al. 2023a, who prompted with invalid reasoning steps in the exemplars. Zhang 2023c found mistakes in exemplar rationales do not cause significant drops.
 quote: "LLMs can generate coherent reasoning steps and achieve over 80-90% of the performance, though prompted with invalid reasoning steps in the exemplars."
 also: "CoT techniques help compel the model to conduct reasoning rather than teaching it how to accomplish reasoning"
 where: p.6

4. ReAct-style interleaving of thought, action and observation bridges reasoning and acting (qualitative; no numbers). This is the survey's whole treatment of ReAct.
 number: none
 quote: "The gap between reasoning and action is bridged by combining interleaving thought, action, and observation (Yao et al., 2022; Khattab et al., 2022; Shinn et al., 2023). ... it has been found that reasoning and acting achieve mutual promotion. Reasoning traces help the model make action plans and handle exceptions, while actions allow the LLM to interface with external sources, such as knowledge bases or environments, to gather additional information for knowledge support."
 where: p.22 (Sec 5.2.3 "Reasoning as CoT")
 related: Xu 2023b (ReWOO) "detached the reasoning process from external observations to reduce token consumption during multiple steps of CoT." AgentBench uses "think" and "Act" steps. Chain-of-action (Zhang & Zhang 2023) uses past action history plus future action plans, so that "decision-making [becomes] a CoT reasoning problem."

5. Tool use is framed as extending the model's ability boundary, for three purposes: action execution, external knowledge acquisition, and reasoning/verification.
 number: none
 quote: "Tool use can be seen as an expansion of a language model's ability boundary, compensating for parametric knowledge for reasoning and grounding the language model's capabilities to interact with environments (Qin et al., 2023b)."
 purposes, verbatim: "Action execution." / "External knowledge acquisition. Retrieval augmentation has been shown so effective that has been regarded as a standard solution to alleviate the factuality drawback (Trivedi et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022)." / "Reasoning and verification. ... Tools that provide accurate, real-time knowledge can help correct reasoning errors"
 tool types listed: knowledge bases, search engines, code interpreters, online models/APIs, applications, databases, bespoke tools. Multi-tool planning "involving depth-first or breadth-first approaches" (Qin 2023b, Liu 2023e).
 where: p.19-20 (Sec 5.1.3)

6. CoT verification without external feedback is unreliable. Gains in self-verification and self-correction papers came from oracles or external tools.
 number: none
 quote: "Huang et al. (2023a) identified that the enhancements observed in CoT verification studies were often facilitated by the utilization of oracles ... In the absence of oracles, LLMs encounter difficulties in rectifying their initial responses solely relying on their inherent capabilities"
 and: "the key to achieving effective CoT verification lies in harnessing external, high-quality feedback for verification. For instance, integrating external tools such as search engines and calculators into the verification process has shown beneficial"
 also: Valmeekam 2023 report over-correction with false positives. CRITIC (Gou 2023a) is tool-interactive critiquing, with search and code interpreter wrapped as text-to-text functions.
 where: p.13

7. CoT drives agent perception, memory and reasoning. Perception as CoT improves action prediction.
 number: none (no figure given)
 quote: "Rawles et al. (2023) found that using the CoT template, 'Answer: Let's think step by step. I see <Screen Caption>, I need to ... ', substantially improves the action prediction accuracy."
 where: p.20. Self-correction from environment feedback (error messages from code or actions) is credited here (Yao 2023b Retroformer, Chen 2023d self-debug).

8. Prompting alone may not suffice for agents. Fine-tuning is the emerging route.
 number: none
 quote: "LLM performance has shown to be sensitive to prompts and there is a lack of evidence that LLM can actually learn domain knowledge from the prompts. Therefore, purely prompting methods may not be adequate to make LLMs generalizable to new domains."
 evidence cited: FireAct (Chen 2023a) fine-tuning "can not only achieve strong generalization and robustness but also improve performance". ToRA (Gou 2023b) trained on "interleaved tool-use data composed of natural language CoT with tool-integrated programs" and got "substantial performance gains" on math. Table 2 lists ReAct as fine-tuned on PaLM-8B and Toolformer as fine-tuned on GPT-J.
 where: p.22-23

9. Program-of-Thoughts and code interpreters decouple computation from reasoning. They give the top reported arithmetic results.
 number: 97.00 (GSM8K), 89.10 (SVAMP)
 setup: Table 1, "best CoT*" as of Oct 2023, model varies per task. Not comparable across rows.
 quote: "GSM8K CSV (Zhou et al., 2023b) 97.00 GPT-4 Code Interpreter" ; "SV AMP PoT (Chen et al., 2022) + SC 89.10 Text-davinci-002"
 other rows: AQuA 70.34 (Natural Program, ChatGPT); CSQA 95.10 and StrategyQA 90.40 (Manual-CoT + SC, PaLM 2); last-letter 92.98 (ChatGPT); Coin Flip 99.90 (Auto-CoT, davinci-002).
 PoT quote: "PoT uses language models to generate both text and programming language statements, which can be executed on a program interpreter to decouple complex computation from reasoning and language understanding."
 where: p.8, p.10

10. Manual-CoT does not help commonsense reasoning at davinci-002 scale. It helps at PaLM 540B or with self-consistency.
 number: none (Fig 3 values not extractable)
 quote: "While Manual-CoT fails to yield performance gains in commonsense reasoning, the optimization of reasoning techniques, such as self-consistency answer aggregation ... and automatic exemplar construction ... reveals the potential of CoT"
 where: p.7

11. Language agents versus RL agents (Table 3).
 quote: "language agents distinguish themselves from RL agents by leveraging commonsense priors embedded in LLMs. These priors reduce dependence on human annotation and trial-and-error learning"
 limit: "language agents face challenges in evolving their parameters in response to environmental changes, primarily because they are predominantly adapted to environments through prompts or the heavy costs of fine-tuning"
 where: p.16

12. General agent framework: a user instruction, an episode of turns, environment interaction, and tools. Other frameworks are named.
 - Wang 2023b: profile, memory, planning and action modules.
 - Xi 2023: brain, perception, action.
 - Zhou 2023d: planning, memory, tool use, multi-agent communication.
 - CoALA (Sumers 2023): working vs long-term memory, internal vs external actions, interactive loop of planning and execution.
 Environment handling splits into "environment parsing" (OCR, icon detectors producing text or HTML) and "multimodal perception". Agents are split into autonomous (AutoGPT, BabyAGI, AgentGPT) and communicative (generative agents, CAMEL, MetaGPT, debate).
 quote: "recent technical research ... tends to follow the line of the conceptual framework by prompting LLMs to imitate the agent processes such as perception, memory, and reasoning. The basic assumption is that LLMs have already captured world knowledge to some extent"
 where: p.18-19

13. Agent memory: short-term is chat or action history, long-term is retrieved. Two efficient-storage approaches.
 - Tree search: MemWalker, GITM sub-goal tree, Park 2023 reflection tree.
 - Vector retrieval: AgentSims.
 quote: "Due to the significant temporal character, short-term memory raises little storage concern." Long-term is split into "procedural memory ... semantic memory ... and episodic memory".
 where: p.21-22

14. Reasoning-format shifts beyond a linear chain, with no quantitative results given.
 - Program-of-Thoughts, Tab-CoT, Tree-of-Thoughts, Graph-of-Thoughts (Besta), Recursion-of-Thought, Skeleton-of-Thought.
 - Aggregation: self-consistency by majority vote. Wang 2022 found "the best way to improve task performance is sampling rationale in the output space."
 - PRM vs ORM: "process supervision significantly outperforms outcome supervision." PRM800K is "800,000 step-level human feedback labels".
 where: p.10-12

15. ChemCrow is the worked example of a CoT-driven tool agent.
 number: 18
 quote: "Through the integration of 18 expert-designed tools, the LLM's performance in chemistry-related tasks is significantly improved."
 setup: GPT-4 per Table 2. Qualitative; it plans and executes syntheses of an insect repellent and three organocatalysts, and it found a novel chromophore.
 where: p.15

16. MGSM and prompting-pattern details, for completeness.
 - MGSM: "250 grade-school math problems that have been translated into ten linguistically diverse languages."
 - Zero-shot CoT: "Let's think step by step".
 - Plan-and-Solve prompt: "Let's first understand the problem and devise a plan to solve the problem. Then, let's carry out the plan and solve the problem step by step".
 - Auto-CoT: cluster problems, then sample one per cluster with Zero-Shot-CoT.
 - Active-Prompt: choose the most uncertain questions.
 - APE and OPRO: automatic instruction search.
 where: p.8-10, 13

LIMITS
- It is a survey. There are no new experiments, and almost all numbers are quoted from other papers and are not controlled comparisons.
- Treatment of ReAct and tool use is brief and descriptive. It gives no ReAct benchmark numbers, no tool-calling API or function-calling schema detail, and no failure analysis of tool agents.
- The cutoff is October 2023. Later work is missing: reasoning models (o1-style), native function calling, MCP, and long-context agents.
- The authors concede that agent safety is "underexplored" and that the definition of language agent safety "has not yet reached an agreement".
- They concede that evaluation is hard: success is "task-specific and ambiguous", execution feedback is "not always accessible", and external judges bring model bias.
- They say the interpretability benefit is limited: "fully characterizing the model's computations supporting an answer still presents an open challenge".
- Open challenges they list: generalization to unseen domains, redundant interactions (agents use "only a limited number of log steps"), customizable agents, scaling, safety, and evaluation.
- The ReAct row in Table 2 is labelled "Communicative" and "Finetuning" with PaLM-8B. That is the survey's own classification, and it may not match how the note describes ReAct.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
CoT: Wei et al. 2022/2023b, Nye et al. 2022. Zero-shot CoT: Kojima et al. 2023. Self-consistency: Wang et al. 2023f. ReAct: Yao et al. 2022. Reflexion: Shinn et al. 2023. Toolformer: Schick et al. 2023. Program-of-Thoughts: Chen et al. 2022. Tree-of-Thoughts: Yao et al. 2023a. Graph-of-Thoughts: Besta et al. 2023. Auto-CoT: Zhang et al. 2023c. Active-Prompt: Diao et al. 2023. APE: Zhou et al. 2023f. OPRO: Yang et al. 2023a. Plan-and-Solve: Wang et al. 2023d. CRITIC: Gou et al. 2023a. ToRA: Gou et al. 2023b. FireAct: Chen et al. 2023a. CoALA: Sumers et al. 2023. Other agent surveys: Wang et al. 2023b, Xi et al. 2023. Generative Agents: Park et al. 2023. Theory: Prystawski & Goodman 2023. Self-correction critique: Huang et al. 2023a, Valmeekam et al. 2023. Process supervision: Lightman et al. 2023. Prior CoT surveys: Chu et al. 2023, Qiao et al. 2023, Lu et al. 2023. Tool learning: Qin et al. 2023b.

CODE
No code in the source. The only literal prompt templates are the quoted prompts above and the ReAct trace in Fig 1: "Search[Colorado orogeny ]" ... "Finish[1,800 to 7,000 ft]". The CoT definition is formal: E = [(x1,r1,y1)◦...◦(xn,rn,yn)] (Eq. 1), Zero-Shot-CoT is Eq. 2, and Few-Shot-CoT is Eq. 3 (p.4).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): language agent framework with CoT in perception, memory and reasoning. It shows a ReAct-style trace answering the Colorado orogeny question (Search / Finish steps, with the model correcting itself from "High Plains" to "High Plains (United States)"). It is the fastest picture of CoT-to-agent.
- Fig 2 (p.4): CoT vs direct reasoning.
- Fig 3 (p.7): performance on seven reasoning tasks. Bars are not extractable as text.
- Fig 5 (p.11): CoT formulations (CoT, PoT, Tab-CoT, ToT, GoT).
- Fig 7 (p.16): agent application areas.
- Fig 8 (p.18): general language agent framework. The loop is instruction, agent (CoT, decision making), tool and environment interaction, with memory and state.
- Fig 9 (p.21): multimodal perception methods.
- Tables: Table 1 (p.8) best CoT per task. Table 2 (p.17) is a technical comparison of about 27 agents with columns for memory, methodology, tools (Web / Code / Other). Table 3 (p.17) compares RL agents with language agents.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
- Figure text (Fig 1 HTML snippet) and the Table 2 and Table 1 layout are partly garbled in extraction. Table 2 cell alignment is approximate.
- Fig 3 numeric values are not recoverable from the text.
- The "20 billion" threshold is hedged ("preferably") and rests on Tay et al. 2022. It is not the authors' own finding.
